name: Endless ambient texture from one looping MIDI clip: seeded random notes in a gap-free scale, per-note chance below 50%, randomised velocity/humanise, slow sine pad, scale-degree fifth chording and stereo/granular/reverb chain
goal: Make a single looping MIDI clip never sound the same twice. Generate seeded random notes locked to a scale without half steps (major pentatonic; Dorian also liked), in a mid register (pitch range ~2–3) with long durations. Then lower each note's play chance below 50% (or below 30% for sparse, many-voice clips) and randomise chance, velocity and timing deviation. Play a soft sine pad (~1 s attack, ~6 s release, so sparse notes overlap), add a scale-aware chord effect (scale degree +4 = fifth on every triggered note), then stereo doubling, a parallel echo, a stereo pitch-loop/micro-delay, granular delay (spray up, frequency down) and a big long reverb. For Polyrhythm Studio-style generative scheduling: probability per note, not a fixed sequence.

source.title: The Secret to Endless Ambient Textures in Ableton Live
source.transcript_note: Patreon/subscribe CTA dropped. Host-specific generator UI mapped to generic per-note probability.

prerequisites: Sequencer/clip with per-note probability (Web Audio: scheduler that rolls Math.random() < p per note, implementation note)
Seeded random note generator or a hand-made scale-locked note list
Sine/pad synth with slow attack, long release, enough voices
Chord/interval generator, stereo doubler/chorus, echo, granular delay, long reverb

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: Gap-free scale such as major pentatonic or Dorian

outputs.name: endless_ambient_loop
outputs.description: Evolving soundscape that varies on every loop pass

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
When you add voices/density after setting chance, chance resets to 100%; re-apply it.
'Fit to scale' re-quantises notes after changing scale.
Sparse clips need long releases so notes still connect.
DAW shortcut and device names are host-specific; the recipe is portable.

steps.action: Create a looping MIDI clip and set its scale (e.g. C minor, then switch to major pentatonic or Dorian; scales without half steps suit generative work). Use fit-to-scale after any scale change.
Generate seeded random notes: set density, pitch register around 2–3 (mid range rather than 0–1), longer durations for smooth pad-like notes, and the number of voices.
steps.expect: Random in-scale notes across the loop

steps.action: Randomise velocities and add deviation/humanise so timing and dynamics wiggle off the grid.

Select all notes and set chance (play probability) to about 50%, then randomise it so some notes play ~90% and others ~15%. With many voices/density keep chance below 50% or even 30%. Re-apply after regenerating.
steps.expect: Every loop pass plays a different subset

steps.action: Sound: simple sine pad (second oscillator off), attack just over 1 s, release ~6 s, extra voices for overlaps.
steps.expect: Notes float in and out and overlap

steps.action: Add a chord/interval effect before the synth in scale mode with a scale degree of 4 (perfect fifth), so every triggered note becomes a power-fifth.
Effects: stereo doubler, parallel echo, a stereo pitch-loop/micro-delay for randomised stereo, granular delay (raise spray, lower frequency) for glitchy texture, then a long-decay reverb.

verification: Two consecutive loop passes play audibly different note subsets.
All notes remain in the chosen scale after fit-to-scale.
With chance <30% the texture is sparse but continuous thanks to the 6 s release.
Every triggered note sounds with its fifth when the chord effect is on.
